messages:
Maria H: FYI, saw sustained egress throttling on SFO edge starting ~11:42 UTC. LAX->SFO slices spiked and warm-pool spinups failed. Logs show high egress QPS + repeated BGP withdraws. ops-bot fired alert. :eyes:

ops-bot: alert: SFO egress-backpressure detected (prefix: sfo-edge-*)
- metric: egress_queue_length > 500 for 3m
- peers: 3/6 transient withdraws
- sample logs:
```
WARN 11:42:12 egress: throttle applied to sfo-edge-pool-3, queue 642
ERROR 11:43:01 route: BGP withdraw to 10.34.0.0/24
```

Ajay P: impact? is this manifesting as API errors or just latency?

Maria H: mostly tail latency and some 503s for long-generations hitting sfo. Hosted API frontends routed more to sfo so user-visible latency rose ~300-800ms p95, a few retries surfaced as 503. Dedicated workloads with region pinning unaffected.

Ken: can we do a partial traffic-shift to reduce SFO egress without blowing up downstream latency? propose progressive weight shifts + keep KV cache affinity for session tokens. Quick command I used in dry-run:
```
./traffic-shift --from sfo --to iad,ams --percent 25 --preserve-cache
```

Lucy: also flagging that automatic warm-pool scaling hit quota limits when egress delayed handshake — need runbook step to pre-warm reserve capacity for critical regions. Add detection to alert earlier (queue > 200 for 2m).

Thomas: cost note — moving traffic to IAD/AMS will increase egress and inter-region bandwidth costs. We should add an emergency cost-override in the playbook so SREs know who signs off for >$X/hr spikes.

Ajay P: agree. Also we should avoid full cutover; do weight-based gradual shift + canary to validate latencies. devex-bot, can we add a canary route policy?

devex-bot: suggested template: canary route with 5% -> 20% over 5m increments, auto-rollback if p95 increases >200ms or error rate >1%. Template link: /ops/policies/canary-route-template (draft)

Ken: adding a quick ops snippet for manual weight adjust (for runbook):
```
# change weights for traffic-router
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/traffic-shift \
  -d '{"from":"sfo","to":["iad","ams"],"percent":20,"dry_run":false}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN'
```

Maria H: action items I propose (short):
- MARIA: own runbook PR to add "egress-priority-shift" section, include thresholds, scripts, and cost-override text (target EOD)
- AJAY: add alert rules: queue >200 for 2m, queue >500 for 1m escalate, BGP withdraw count >2 (due 24h)
- KEN: add automation script for gradual weight shifts with dry-run and canary checks (start tomorrow)
- LUCY: update warm-pool quotas/playbook to pre-warm reserve slices and test in staging (48h)
- THOMAS: draft emergency cost signoff flow and numbers (48h)

Lucy: also add a test section: simulate egress backpressure in staging with `tc` + BGP withdraw emulator so the runbook steps are validated.

Thomas: created INF ticket for cost policy: INF-3245 (link internal)

ops-bot: created incident task INF-3244: runbook egress-priority-shift addendum, assigned to Maria H, due 2026-03-20.

Ajay P: For post-incident notes, suggest we record root-cause as external eBGP flap + provider-level egress policing, not internal VM CPU. Keep troubleshooting checklist: BGP peers, provider NOC, prefix acceptance, egress QPS.

Maria H: +1. I'll include RCA template and timeline in the PR. Also adding a short postmortem doc with impact numbers (p95 delta, retries, affected customers list).

Ken: one more ops tweak — add graceful fallback that preserves KV cache affinity for 10m after shift to avoid large quality regressions for chat sessions. I'll prototype today.

Maria H: thanks all. I'll open the PR and post links here when ready. If anyone hits urgent regressions, DM me and @ops oncall. :thumbsup:
